name: How often should a pool be resurfaced in Southern California?

mainEntity.name: What is the realistic resurfacing interval for plaster, quartz, and pebble finishes in hot, sunny climates?
mainEntity.text: What is the realistic resurfacing interval for plaster, quartz, and pebble finishes in hot, sunny climates?

acceptedAnswer.text: The resurfacing interval is not fixed because it depends on the finish and how the pool is maintained. Standard plaster generally needs replacement sooner than quartz or pebble, which are built for longer service life. In a climate like Southern California, sunlight, heat, and hard water can accelerate wear, scaling, and staining if chemistry is not managed carefully. Heavy use also shortens the life of any finish. A homeowner should think of resurfacing as part of a long-term maintenance cycle rather than a one-time cosmetic project. If the surface is still smooth, cleanable, and watertight, it may be worth waiting. If it is rough, patched, or visually failing, the pool is usually telling you the finish has reached the end of its useful life.
acceptedAnswer.description: Resurfacing frequency depends on finish type, water chemistry, sunlight, and usage. Standard plaster usually wears out sooner than quartz or pebble finishes, which tend to last longer. In Southern California, strong sun and hard water can shorten any finish’s life if maintenance is inconsistent.
